question_text: Outline a security advantage of letting a web server access a central ratings database rather than sending database credentials to every browser. Explain the roles of browser and server.
adaptation_rationale: Retain client/server roles and protected central data access without claiming server code is automatically secure. Scenario and wording rewritten; source reasoning retained only within supported 2027 scope.
solution: The browser sends a limited request to the server; server-side code uses credentials retained on the server to perform permitted database operations. Users do not receive unrestricted database credentials, reducing credential exposure, although authentication and safe query handling are still needed.

marking_points.criterion: Browser requests service rather than receiving database credentials.
Server performs permitted central database operations with credentials held server-side.
Links this division to reduced exposure/unauthorized direct database access; no absolute security claim.
